# 2 Chronicles Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** After this, the Moabites, Ammonites, and some of the Meunites came to wage war against Jehoshaphat.

**2** Messengers came and told Jehoshaphat, "A vast army is coming against you from the other side of the Dead Sea, from Edom. They are already at Hazazon-tamar" (that is, En-gedi).

**3** Alarmed, Jehoshaphat resolved to seek the LORD, and he proclaimed a fast for all Judah.

**4** The people of Judah came together to seek help from the LORD — from every town in Judah they came to seek Him.

**5** Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem at the LORD's temple, in front of the new courtyard.

**6** He prayed: "LORD, God of our ancestors, are You not the God who is in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and might are in Your hand, and no one can stand against You.

**7** Our God, didn't You drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham, Your friend?

**8** They have lived in it and built a sanctuary in it for Your name, saying,

**9** 'If disaster strikes us — whether war, judgment, plague, or famine — we will stand before this temple and before You, for Your name is in this temple, and we will cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear and save.'

**10** But now look at what the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir are doing — the very nations You wouldn't let Israel invade when they came out of Egypt, so they turned away and didn't destroy them.

**11** See how they repay us! They're coming to drive us out of the possession You gave us.

**12** Our God, won't You judge them? We have no power to face this vast army that is attacking us. We don't know what to do, but our eyes are on You."

**13** All the men of Judah, with their wives, children, and little ones, stood before the LORD.

**14** Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite and descendant of Asaph, as he stood in the assembly.

**15** He said, "Listen, King Jehoshaphat and all who live in Judah and Jerusalem! This is what the LORD says to you: 'Don't be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army. For the battle is not yours, but God's.

**16** Tomorrow, march down against them. They will be climbing up by the Pass of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the gorge in the Desert of Jeruel.

**17** You will not have to fight this battle. Take your positions, stand firm, and see the deliverance the LORD will give you, Judah and Jerusalem. Don't be afraid; don't be discouraged. Go out and face them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you.'"

**18** Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem fell down before the LORD in worship.

**19** Then some Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stood up and praised the LORD, the God of Israel, with very loud voices.

**20** Early in the morning they left for the Desert of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and people of Jerusalem! Have faith in the LORD your God, and you will stand firm. Have faith in His prophets, and you will succeed."

**21** After consulting the people, he appointed singers to walk ahead of the army, singing to the LORD and praising Him in sacred splendor, saying: "Give thanks to the LORD, for His faithful love endures forever."

**22** As they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who were invading Judah, and they were defeated.

**23** The Ammonites and Moabites turned on the men from Mount Seir and completely destroyed them. After they finished slaughtering the men of Seir, they turned on each other.

**24** When the men of Judah reached the lookout point over the desert and looked toward the enemy forces, they saw only dead bodies lying on the ground — not a single survivor.

**25** Jehoshaphat and his men went to carry off the plunder, and they found among the bodies vast quantities of equipment, clothing, and valuables — more than they could take. It took three days to collect the plunder, there was so much.

**26** On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah (Blessing), for there they praised the LORD. That is why it is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.

**27** Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned joyfully to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, for the LORD had given them cause to celebrate over their enemies.

**28** They entered Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets and went to the LORD's temple.

**29** The fear of God fell on all the surrounding kingdoms when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

**30** And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.

**31** So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

**32** He walked in the ways of his father Asa, never straying from them; he did what was right in the LORD's eyes.

**33** The high places, however, were not removed, and the people still had not set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.

**34** The other events of Jehoshaphat's reign, from beginning to end, are written in the annals of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel.

**35** Later, King Jehoshaphat of Judah made an alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel, who was guilty of wickedness.

**36** He agreed with him to build a fleet of trading ships. They built the ships at Ezion-geber.

**37** But Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD will destroy what you have built." The ships were wrecked and never made it to Tarshish.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **20:12**: "We don't know what to do, but our eyes are on You" — this is the most honest prayer in the Bible. No strategy, no backup plan, no false confidence. Just raw dependence. And it works.

- **20:15**: "The battle is not yours, but God's" — seven words that changed the battle. Jehoshaphat's army doesn't need to fight. They need to show up and watch.

- **20:21**: Singers before soldiers. Praise before battle. This is either insanity or the deepest possible theology of warfare. The Chronicler clearly thinks it's the latter.

- **20:22**: "As they began to sing and praise" — the timing is precise. God acts the moment worship begins. Not before, not after. When Israel sings, God fights.


— PNEUMA
